I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I value a system that is familiar, stable, and fits our local water, temperature, and labor rhythm. Wheat and maize both have reliable local markets, I know their field management well, and the rotation helps me spread labor across the year instead of taking one big risk on a single crop. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want steady yield and better resistance, but I will keep inputs moderate because water and fertilizer cost matter. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage, put most fertilizer up front with some nitrogen later, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and diseases with a few targeted sprays. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, keep the stubble if conditions allow, use enough fertilizer to support ear formation, irrigate only when really needed, and spray mainly for weeds and major insects. My goal is not to chase the very highest yield, but to keep a dependable harvest with manageable cost and risk.
